gate: C++ reference corpus (SPRINT-21): Debian abseil 20240722.0 orig tarball, 811 .cc/.h files (+5 python pack files, +1 C pack file)

2_parse_honesty.packs_note: 5 python test utilities + 1 C compat file (absl/base/c_header_test.c) join the C-family files -- the multi-pack scan is part of the honest measurement
2_parse_honesty.boundary_note: 646/817 analyzed files carry at least one raw-source parse error (pinned): 581 carry the macro-namespace class (ABSL_NAMESPACE_BEGIN/END expand to `namespace absl {`), 207+ the ABSL_ATTRIBUTE_*/ABSL_FLAG_* macro families, token pasting and X-macros in the test support, ~20 residual. No canonical C++ corpus parses 100% clean as-written (catch2 3.7.1 135/427, spdlog 1.15.2 74/132); the pinned count IS the kill-switch -- a grammar or tool regression moves it.

4_resolver_honesty.note: abseil's canonical ROOT-RELATIVE quoted include style resolves only the same-directory payload forms under the file-relative rule; every unresolved system/macro/root-relative include stays recorded-and-unresolved.

5_rule_honesty.note: OC003=0: no same-dir include cycle exists in this corpus (the resolver-cycle semantics are pinned by the lang gate corpus B). OC005=1: a PYTHON-pack finding (copts.py's GccStyleFilterAndCombine -- the python pack's named-bind semantics), measured, not fabricated. No manifest tier exists for C++: the supply block is absent and the meta says so.

6_header_routing.note: every .h routed through the approved treatment: the literal-namespace header sniffs cpp, the macro-namespace headers are inconclusive (both grammars error on the raw macro tokens) and the ROOT DEFAULT claims them for cpp (the corpus carries .cc sources).
